title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: In 2020, Ministry of Labour, Immigration and Population (MOLIP) opened 4 new Migrant Resource Centres (MRCs) in 4 different States and Regions, in addition to its continued operations of 6 MRCs in Government Labour Exchange offices of 6 cities across country. These MRCs provides information to aspiring migrants about recruitment agencies, procedures for migration, details of necessary documents and information about job opportunities and the working and living conditions in countries of destination. The MOLIP improved the data collection system of the Complaints Mechanism to generate more comprehensive information on complaints with sex disaggregated, job sector, country, type of complaint and the progress on resolving them. Labour Organizations (LO) and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) increased their services at Migrant Centres in 12 places across different States and Regions including border areas with Thailand and China to ensure that workers seeking jobs overseas can get up to date information and counselling before making a decision about migrating, and can seek support on migration protection. According to data provided by these Migrant Centres, a total of 50,940 beneficiaries used these services which constitute of women 44% and men 56% during Jan 2020 to June 2021. Migrant Centres also provides the legal assistance to migrant workers who faced abuses and exploitation during their migration process and hundreds of cases have been resolved. The CSOs network and LO network for Myanmar migrants responded to legal issues for migrants as COVID worsens in countries of destination in 2020. In 2020, 272 licensed recruitment agencies out of 300 voluntarily signed up Code of Conduct from Myanmar Overseas Employment Agencies Federation (MOEAF). MOEAF's Code Compliance and Monitoring Committee completed two country guidelines for Japan and Malaysia to use as reference guide for monitoring on compliance of overseas employment agencies on their Code of Conduct With support of European Union (EU), the ILO provided technical support to Ministry of Labour, Immigration and Population (MOLIP) for the development and implementation of 4 new Migrant Resource centres (MRCs) in Labour Exchange Offices (LEOs) in 2020. The ILO also trained government officials on providing services to migrant workers and appointed 4 consultants for these MRCs to provide going technical assistance. With support of Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), ILO continued to provide technical support to MRCs in 6 government Labour Exchange. With support of Livelihoods and Food Security Fund (LIFT), the ILO, in 2020, provided a series of capacity building trainings for government officials to strengthen their capacity on providing services in better and systematic way for its complaints mechanism, which includes trainings on complaints mechanism to settle on labour and recruitment disputes more effectively and timely. In collaboration of DFAT, LIFT and EU, the ILO supported Migrants Centres of Labour Organizations and Civil Society Organziations providing support services for migrant workers and their families in 7 different States/Regions. The ILO strengthened coordination between media, CSOs, Labour organizations and government to ensure more accurate reporting on migration, and to increase channels to disseminate safe migration information.A series of policy-oriented publications on Extension of social protection to internal migrants in the informal sector and Assessment Study on the Skills of Returned Migrant Workers were also produced to strengthen the knowledge base of stakeholders. The ILO provided technical assistance to MOEAF for development of Code of Conduct, and continued providing technical inputs to Code Compliance and Monitoring Committee on ongoing process of monitoring and ranking the overseas employment agencies on their compliance of Code of Conduct.
